channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [7] Giant magnetic moment increase by ultrafast laser light
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: John Kay Dewhurst, Sam Shallcross

Authors: Sangeeta Sharma, Deepika Gill, Jyoti Krishna, Eddie Harris-Lee, John Kay Dewhurst, Sam Shallcross

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of ultrafast dynamics in magnetic van der Waals systems like CrSBr and CrI3.

Tags: #magnetism #vanderWaals #ultrafast

Abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73780-z It is well established that intense laser pulses can demagnetize magnetic matter; however, the inverse process of magnetic moment enhancement by ultrafast laser light is generally precluded. Here, Sharma and coauthors show how combining a spin-orbit-induced spin texture with strong optical drive in CrSBr and CrI3 leads to substantial increase in magnetic moment.

item.title: [7] Ferron-driven photoferroic hysteresis in van der Waals CuInP2S6
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Edwin Hang Tong Teo, Ranjan Singh

Authors: Sambhu Jana, Baolong Zhang, Sobhan Subhra Mishra, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigation of quasiparticle dynamics in van der Waals ferroelectrics/multiferroics.

Tags: #vanderWaals #quasiparticle #ferroelectric

Abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 03 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73771-0 The authors identify ferron quasiparticles in layered CuInP2S6 and show that they drive light induced photocurrent hysteresis, offering a route toward advanced optoelectronic and neuromorphic devices.
